body: Wednesday, July 01 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed held rates steady at its June meeting with the dot plot signaling a hawkish shift — higher for longer is now the official posture. Inflation reportedly topped 4%, keeping Warsh's Fed boxed in despite political pressure from Trump to ease. Fiscal deficits remain large; Reuters flagged the market boom running on a "large deficit model." The 10Y yield sits at 4.47% (+2 bps vs 4W), the 2Y at 4.14% (prior close, +9 bps vs 4W), leaving a +30 bps term spread — the curve is positive but still flat by historical standards, and yields are grinding higher, not lower.

New / Most Important: Q2 closed with the best quarterly performance in six years per NBC News. However, Q3 opened with a notable rotation: Meta advancing while semiconductors slide, and Russell 2000 (↑3.6% vs 4W) sharply outperforming Nasdaq 100 (↓2.4% vs 4W). The Russell/Nasdaq ratio is ↑6.2% — breadth is expanding away from mega-cap tech. Multiple outlets warned that US economic performance "no longer aligns" with the stock market, and bears see bullish tailwinds "reversing." SpaceX's IPO reportedly coincided with $2 trillion in tech market cap losses — a potential capital reallocation event of historic scale.

Playbook ✓: Hawkish Fed hold with sticky inflation keeps USD firm and bonds under pressure — textbook. Oil weakness (WTI at 68.28, ↓27.2% vs 4W) on US-Iran progress is disinflationary but hasn't changed the Fed's calculus yet.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The SpaceX IPO month is a genuinely structural event. Tech giants losing $2 trillion while a single IPO absorbs institutional flows represents a capital flow regime change — money is physically leaving the crowded AI/mega-cap trade and rotating into the "real asset" and "new frontier" private-to-public pipeline. This is NOT a normal sector rotation; it's a liquidity event where new supply (SpaceX shares) is being funded by liquidation of existing tech holdings. The Russell outperformance confirms this broadening is real, not just noise. The risk is that this rotation becomes self-reinforcing: as mega-cap tech underperforms, passive flows slow, creating a reflexive downdraft in the very stocks that carried the indices. Watch the Nasdaq 100's underperformance carefully — if it accelerates, the "large deficit model" stock market boom could fracture along factor lines, with value/small-cap up and growth/momentum down simultaneously.

Macro Stance: The ECB remains in a cautious hold posture, but the case for patience (not tightening) strengthened materially this week. Lagarde noted that Europe's economic resilience gives the ECB "greater room to move rates." Fiscal conditions across the bloc are stable but not expansionary.

New / Most Important: Eurozone June inflation fell more than expected to 2.8% as the energy shock faded — this was the dominant headline across multiple outlets. ECB's Wunsch said further tightening would require "stronger second-round effects," effectively taking additional hikes off the table. The euro slipped on the data as markets priced in a more dovish trajectory. The UK stock market continues losing listed companies — a structural hollowing-out of London's equity ecosystem.

Playbook ✓: Disinflation driven by energy base effects is precisely what consensus expected for H2 2026. ECB patience is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The speed of the inflation decline (below expectations) could pull forward the first ECB cut timeline, creating a meaningful EUR/USD divergence trade if the Fed stays hawkish while the ECB pivots. This would be the first genuine transatlantic policy divergence since the synchronized tightening began.

Macro Stance: The PBOC's overnight framework is in its first week: reverse repos debuted at 1.25% (Reuters, [Jun 28]), below the 1.35% a Bloomberg survey expected ([Jun 25]), and the cash injection was then doubled at an unchanged rate (Reuters, [Jun 29]). Quantity signals conflict: TradingView reports liquidity added [Jun 30] while BigGo Finance tallies a drain of over 1.16 trillion yuan [Jun 30] — daily top-ups against larger maturities, so overnight money is cheaper but the liquidity stock is not expanding. A PBOC adviser sees a potential rate cut but calls for targeted aid instead (Bloomberg, [Jun 24]). The yuan midpoint was set weaker for a third day (SCMP, [Jun 24]) and options traders have turned bullish on the dollar (Bloomberg, [Jun 30]). Prices stay split: May CPI rose only 1.2% (China Daily, [Jun 10]) while factory-gate inflation hit a near four-year high (Reuters, [Jun 9]).

PMIs & Activity: The growth pulse turned up in June, narrowly. The official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.3 (Reuters, [Jun 29]) from a flat 50 in May, on tech export demand (CNBC, [Jun 29]); non-manufacturing rose to 50.2 (Reuters, [Jun 29]). The private gauge capped its strongest quarter since late 2020 (Reuters, [Jun 30]), yet June grew less than expected (Bloomberg, [Jun 30]): a high average with momentum fading. May's hard data show the split: output growth quickened to 4.5% (China Daily, [Jun 16]) and exports jumped 19.4% (AP News, [Jun 9]), but retail sales fell 0.6% (Il Sole 24 Ore, [Jun 15]) and fixed-asset investment fell 4.1% in five months (Macau Business, [Jun 16]); industrial profit growth slowed for the first time in six months as weak domestic demand bit (Times of India, [Jun 27]).

Credit Impulse: Total social financing grew 7.7% in May (CGTN, [Jun 12]) and topped forecasts (Bloomberg, [Jun 12]), but new loans missed as the property slump curbed demand (Reuters, [Jun 12]): the beat is government bonds, the miss is private demand. The PBOC is urging banks to lend because demand remains weak (Reuters, [Jun 26]). With debt above 300% of GDP (UPI, [Jun 29]), the household and private-firm impulse is still negative.

Property: June's first datapoint is poor: resale home prices fell faster, a private survey shows (Reuters, [Jun 30]), after new home prices fell at a faster pace in May (Reuters, [Jun 15]). Real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May (GMK Center, [Jun 18]). State capital is replacing private balance sheets: Shenzhen Metro's chairman now also chairs Vanke (BigGo Finance, [Jun 30]) and state developers are powering Shenzhen construction (Nikkei Asia, [Jun 29]), while Country Garden paid over 2.8 billion yuan in the half-year after its offshore restructuring (BigGo Finance, [Jun 30]). The private end is still breaking: Beijing land sales plunged 66% (Caixin, [Jun 25]) and the Evergrande Property Services stake sale collapsed (Caixin, [Jun 26]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The 62.5 billion yuan third batch of trade-in funds (Global Times, [Jun 26]) is small against a retail contraction, and the State Council reviewed AI, trade and carbon plans (Dimsum Daily, [Jun 29]) with no demand package. Trade is where policy moves: the EU and China set an October deadline to reset ties (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]) over a €360bn deficit (The Guardian, [Jun 29]); Beijing and Washington agreed a trade council on tariffs (Global Times, [Jun 25]); and China imposed a 73.5% preliminary tariff on Canadian pea starch (Global News, [Jun 30]) and listed 20 Japanese entities for export controls (Reuters, [Jun 29]). The NYT casts China as a relative winner from the Strait of Hormuz crisis [Jun 29].

Markets & Flows: Hong Kong shares fell 11% in the first half for lack of an AI play (SCMP, [Jun 30]), and Chinese stocks trail the AI boom by the most since 2001 (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]), with the MSCI China index down over 15% this year (BigGo Finance, [Jun 30]). Onshore is bifurcated: ChiNext surged 35% in the half while nearly 70% of A-shares declined (BigGo Finance, [Jun 30]). The capital wall is rising: curbs on higher-yielding offshore debt (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]) and on TRS (SCMP, [Jun 24]), and major banks suspended individual gold trading (SCMP, [Jun 25]). Adam Tooze's Chartbook calls this China's "walled-in wealth", cut off from the AI boom.

New / Most Important: The June PMIs are the first upturn in the growth pulse in months, and the composition is the story: manufacturing at 50.3 on tech exports, services barely positive, and a private gauge missing June forecasts, while resale prices fell faster the same day. Beijing's response is stealth easing, a 1.25% overnight rate it would not even publish (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]), not a demand package, and walled-in savings go to bonds and gold rather than spending.

Playbook ✓: Property drag, weak consumption, no headline rate cut and a managed yuan drift are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The consensus wanted a mid-year stimulus pivot; instead an export-led PMI sits on a negative private credit impulse and falling home prices, so China exports its excess supply. Transmission runs three ways. European exporters face a record deficit and an October deadline, a direct risk to European industrials. Construction-linked bulk demand fades with real-estate investment down 16.2%, a drag on AUD and iron ore that export PMIs do not offset. And Bloomberg sees fuel export curbs lifted on ample supplies [Jun 30], more barrels for an oil market where WTI is already down 27.2% in four weeks. Until loan growth, not bond issuance, re-accelerates, Hong Kong rallies are flows, not fundamentals.

Macro Stance: The BoJ's dovish personnel revamp under PM Takaichi's appointees has cast serious doubt on further rate hikes. Yen hit a 40-year low at 162 per dollar. Japan spent $74 billion on intervention but CNBC correctly noted "the real battle is with the Fed" — as long as the US-Japan rate gap persists, intervention is burning reserves for temporary relief.

New / Most Important: This is a structural breakdown in the BoJ's credibility cycle. The BoJ is now being actively reshaped to be dovish at the exact moment the yen demands hawkishness — this is a political override of central bank independence in real-time. The "line in the sand" on yen intervention is reportedly shifting, meaning authorities are tolerating weaker levels. The Tankan survey surged (strong economy) while the yen collapsed (weak currency) — a classic emerging-market dynamic in a developed-market wrapper. This divergence between strong corporate Japan and collapsing currency is the most important macro dislocation globally right now. Japanese corporates are earning record profits in yen terms while foreign purchasing power of yen assets craters, creating a carry-trade paradise that could end violently if intervention escalates or global risk appetite reverses. MUFG acknowledges the BoJ "can tighten further" but admits the yen may stay weak regardless — the rate gap is simply too wide.

Playbook ✓: Yen weakness on wide rate differentials is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The political capture of the BoJ is NOT priced. Markets assume eventual normalization; the Takaichi regime is actively preventing it.

Macro Stance: The RBA held rates at its latest meeting, with minutes emphasizing policy needs to "remain restrictive." Union inflation expectations flagged as "too high." Hawkish hold remains the posture despite AFR reporting that near-zero rates may be "closer than you think" in the next downturn scenario.

New / Most Important: The RBA warned on the budget's influence on housing ("loan-slide"), signaling fiscal-monetary tension.  |  Playbook ✓: Hawkish hold with sticky services inflation is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The "near-zero rates closer than you think" briefing is a non-trivial signal — the RBA is war-gaming for a sharp downturn scenario even as surface messaging remains hawkish. China's growth pulse matters here given Australia's commodity export dependence: China's real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May and its June PMI upturn is export-led, not construction-led.

Macro Stance: Two data points pull in opposite directions. The June flash put CPI exactly at the NBP target with prices down versus May (Obserwator Gospodarczy, [Jul 1]), the 2.5% print that Parkiet said ends the hike debate [Jun 30] and that ING thinks can open a market bet on cuts in the second half of 2026 [Jun 30]. But the manufacturing PMI collapsed to 46.1 in June against a 49.4 consensus (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 1]), the weakest in many months (Forsal.pl, [Jul 1]) and a sudden slump that surprised even analysts (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 1]). The disinflation is also about to be tested: the CPN fuel package ended and prices jumped (Notes From Poland, [Jul 1]), by about 60 groszy a litre per wPolityce.pl [Jul 1], with Gazeta Prawna's estimate that this could lift inflation toward 3% [Jun 30] now live. GUS put the January median wage at 7447 zł gross, so half of workers earn less (Forsal.pl, [Jul 1]) and Business Insider Polska says inequality is rising again [Jul 1]. NBP data show mortgages cheaper than a year ago (Bankier.pl, [Jul 1]). The NBP keeps a dovish lean that is weighing on the zloty, but a PMI at 46.1 turns the question from inflation to growth.

Markets: Quarter-end flattered Warsaw: the WIG20 gained 7.38% in the second quarter, a third positive quarter in a row (FXMAG, [Jul 1]), and Parkiet reported the exchange higher on Wednesday with gold and silver back to gains [Jul 1]; Modivo led and banks and retail drove the market (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 1]). Tuesday's closes on the card: EPOL 38.61 (-0.3% 1W, -3.6% 4W); PKO 103.14 (-1.2% 1W, +3.1% 4W); Pekao 228.8 (-1.0% 1W); Orlen 126.6 (-1.9% 1W, -12.4% 4W); KGHM 331.25 (-5.3% 1W, -5.6% 4W); PGE 9.44 (-3.0% 1W, -8.2% 4W); Allegro 37.81 (-2.9% 1W, +10.1% 4W); CD Projekt 224.4 (-1.9% 1W, -0.7% 4W); LPP 18280 (-1.1% 1W, -15.1% 4W); Dino 28.4 (-2.4% 1W). Orlen is losing momentum with 120 zł the level that decides direction (Comparic.pl, [Jul 1]) and INNPoland.pl links its fall to the end of CPN [Jul 1]; an analyst sharply raised Allegro's valuation (pb.pl, [Jul 1]). FX: USD/PLN closed at 3.7649 (+0.2% 1W, +3.3% 4W) and EUR/PLN at 4.2969 (+0.5% 1W, +1.5% 4W); EUR/PLN tested 4.30 before the zloty firmed with the market waiting for payrolls (wnp.pl, [Jul 1]), Bankier.pl says the euro broke its psychological barrier and the pound is at 5 zł as surprising inflation and a strong dollar hit the zloty [Jul 1]. Credit: Millennium BH placed 500 mln zł of covered bonds with demand above 830 mln zł (Bankier.pl, [Jul 1]) and MF published the July Treasury bond offer (Strefa Inwestorów, [Jul 1]).

Fiscal & Politics: MF put the cost of the CPN fuel programme at 4.7 bn zł and called it a success (XYZ, [Jul 1]); its end is Tusk's holiday "gift" of dearer fuel in wPolityce.pl's telling [Jul 1]. The spending pressure is immediate: Nowacka demands an 11% raise for teachers and says she will not let up on the finance minister (Bankier.pl, [Jul 1]), health-sector minimum pay rose from July (Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 1]), and the government is closing a corporate loophole with a new tax on liquidations (wnp.pl, [Jul 1]). Interia Biznes sums it up as Poland will not go bankrupt, but things will happen [Jul 1]. The three-euro parcel customs charge started, with Allegro commenting (Money.pl, [Jul 1]). The windfall tax still carries the Senate's up-to-100% amendment (Strefa Inwestorów, [Jun 29]), and KS NGR updated the roadmap for the WIBOR reform (Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, [Jul 1]).

Corporate & Sectors: KGHM will invest 725 mln USD to expand Sierra Gorda in Chile (StockWatch.pl, [Jul 1]), lifting ore throughput to around 60 mln tonnes a year (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 1]). Orlen is tightening control of Energa, which may leave the exchange (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 1]), and opened a bioLNG station in Płock (Parkiet, [Jul 1]) while raising wholesale fuel sharply as the shield ended (Super Biznes, [Jul 1]). PKO BP stopped counting the 800 plus benefit toward creditworthiness (Wyborcza.biz, [Jul 1]), launched instant SEPA euro transfers (CRN Polska, [Jul 1]) and its analysts warn home prices face several catches (Bankier.pl, [Jul 1]); flats above a million are becoming the norm in the Tricity (CEO Magazyn, [Jul 1]). pb.pl says the era of easy growth in mass fashion is over, a test for LPP, Pepco and Modivo [Jul 1]. Nuclear advanced: the Pomeranian voivode approved the second stage of site works (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 1]), though Energetyka24 notes the first plant slips later and the second starts over [Jul 1]. A Chinese EV maker picked Poland for a European launch (TVP World, [Jun 29]).

Geopolitics & Security: The Border Defence Component (KOP) returns to the eastern frontier with the 1st Podlasie Territorial Brigade (Defence24, [Jul 1]), and the president extended the military missions in Iraq and Latvia (Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 1]). The Kyiv rift persists: The Times of India reports Poland cancelled MiG-29 deliveries after a UAV technology snub [Jul 1], the FT reported the Polish opposition seeking to block Ukraine's EU bid [Jun 25], and Polish businesses pressed both capitals to end the quarrel (RTL Today, [Jun 29]).

New / Most Important: The PMI at 46.1 is the week's shock. A 2.5% CPI with a contracting factory sector is a growth problem dressed as a disinflation story, and it arrives the day fuel prices jump 60 groszy, so the NBP faces falling core demand and rising headline risk at once. The zloty's refusal to rally on good inflation says the market already treats a cut cycle as fiscally financed.  |  Playbook ✓: Cut bias intact but growth-driven; favour duration and banks over cyclicals, keep KGHM on hold while it commits 725 mln USD into a falling copper tape, and respect Orlen's 120 zł line.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: A WIG20 up 7.38% on the quarter against a PMI at 46.1; CPI at target while fuel jumps 60 groszy; mortgages cheaper and lending at records while the median wage is 7447 zł.

Macro Stance: India's capital markets are undergoing structural transformation. The NSE and Jio Platforms IPOs, covered by BBC, reveal a changing economy shifting from conglomerate-driven to platform-driven capital formation.

New / Most Important: The NSE IPO is a meta-trade — owning the exchange itself as Indian equity volumes structurally grow. This is reminiscent of owning CME or ICE in early innings. Jio Platforms' listing opens direct foreign access to India's digital infrastructure stack.  |  Playbook ✓: India as EM darling for FDI and portfolio flows remains consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: None today.

Narrative: Bearish: Q3 opened with a sharp rotation out of mega-cap tech — the Nasdaq 100 is ↓2.4% vs 4W while the Russell 2000 is ↑3.6%, and SpaceX's IPO month coincided with $2 trillion in tech market-cap losses. The driver is AI-spending scrutiny, with big tech facing questions ahead of Q2 earnings (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 29]).

Reported: BlackBerry lifted its annual revenue forecast as the QNX unit powered growth (BNN Bloomberg, [Jun 25]) and the stock climbed 20% on Q1 earnings that exceeded expectations (TradingView, [Jun 26]). Guidewire slid despite an earnings beat and a higher outlook (StocksToTrade, [Jun 26]), and Accenture's cut to revenue-growth guidance shocked the tech industry (The Hindu, [Jun 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: IBM — shares jumped 5% after JPMorgan upgraded the stock on software acceleration (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 24]). Fair Isaac — raised guidance to $2.45 billion in revenue (TIKR.com, [Jun 25]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The SpaceX IPO is acting as a liquidity vacuum: institutions are selling mega-cap tech to fund allocations, so the marginal dollar into tech is now zero-sum rather than additive.

Narrative: Mixed: Meta's outperformance within the rotation supports XLC, but the sector sits between gaming weakness and ad-revenue resilience, and AOL's re-IPO shows the listing window open even for legacy brands. The driver is how fast AI turns into ad revenue.
Reported: Prosus' profit got a boost from food delivery, travel bookings and Tencent (Business Day, [Jun 29]).
EPS Upside Watch: Take-Two — an analyst says GTA VI could transform earnings (Benzinga, [Jun 24]), a single-title step-up in revenue and margins.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is becoming a rival for the ad budget, not only a tool for it: OpenAI wants $100bn of ad revenue, though it cannot 'guarantee' brand safety (The Media Leader, [Jun 25]). Brand-safety doubts are what keep that money with the incumbent platforms for now.

Narrative: Bullish: a positive but flat curve (+30 bps 10Y-2Y, 2Y at 4.14%) gives only modest NIM support; the stronger driver is capital markets, with the SpaceX, AOL, NSE and Jio listings feeding underwriting fees and small caps (Russell ↑3.6%) lifting regional banks.

Reported: Jefferies' Q2 earnings missed estimates despite a record investment-banking performance (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 25]), with the bank seeing strength in its deal backlog (Bloomberg, [Jun 25]). Australia's Judo Capital cut FY26 profit guidance after three loans went bad (Stocks Down Under, [Jun 25]). Italy's Banca Ifis cut profit guidance after launching the sale of its NPL business (MarketScreener, [Jun 26]).

EPS Upside Watch: RHB Bank — 2Q profit is seen improving on better margins and treasury income (The Edge Malaysia, [Jun 26]). Singapore banks — higher-for-longer US rates could boost earnings beyond 2026 (The Business Times, [Jun 25]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Credit, not margins, is becoming the swing factor: Judo's loan losses reveal the economy's rapid decline (AFR, [Jun 25]) and Fitch cut its Philippine bank outlook to deteriorating on bad-loan risks (Manila Bulletin, [Jun 25]).

Narrative: Bearish: WTI at 68.28 (↓27.2% vs 4W) has collapsed on US-Iran talks progress, and analysts are dialling down oil forecasts as the Hormuz reopening eases supply concerns (Reuters, [Jun 30]). The majors keep buying assets into the fall.

Reported: Energy Transfer raised its 2026 guidance by $750 million (TIKR.com, [Jun 29]). Worley, the engineering contractor to the energy and resources industries, issued a fresh profit warning (AFR, [Jun 25]). Oil-tanker earnings plunged by $200,000 as more ships returned to Hormuz (Bloomberg.com, [Jun 26]).
EPS Upside Watch: Big oil's trading arms — the majors' secretive trading desks are having an extraordinary year (The Economist, [Jun 28]), a profit source that does not depend on a higher oil price.

⚡ Breaking Convention: This is a supply shock, not demand destruction: China's official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.3 in June and US manufacturing hit a 4-year high in the June flash, yet oil fell 27.2%. Energy equities should find a floor faster than they would in a recession-led slide.

Narrative: Bullish: June manufacturing data were supportive of LTL demand, and small-cap outperformance (Russell ↑3.6%) favours domestically oriented industrials; new orders and the AI-capex spill-over into automation are the drivers.

Reported: AeroVironment soared 28% on an earnings beat as its backlog grew to $1.2 billion (CNBC, [Jun 29]). Maersk lifted guidance on strong demand and higher freight rates (WSJ, [Jun 30]). FedEx Freight's first report beat estimates, but the stock did not move (Barron's, [Jun 26]).

EPS Upside Watch: ArcBest — analysts lifted fair value on freight-recovery views (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 30]). Allegiant — now sees a Q2 profit on falling fuel and the Sun Country merger (Skift, [Jun 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Tariffs are adding to freight earnings rather than cutting them: Maersk raised profit guidance as new US tariffs fuel demand (Financial Times, [Jun 29]), swinging from a loss warning to a USD 4bn profit outlook (Trans.INFO, [Jun 30]). Front-loaded volume can reverse later in the year.
Narrative: Mixed: store closures at a former retail giant and a renewed meme bid show a split consumer; cheaper fuel (WTI ↓27.2%) is the support, tariffs and China the drag.

Reported: Nike beat by $0.08 with revenue above estimates (Investing.com, [Jun 30]) even as China sales dropped 12%, and it expects a $986 million tariff refund (CNBC, [Jun 30]). Carnival beat on revenue and earnings but dipped 5% on weaker Q3 guidance (TIKR.com, [Jun 24]). H&M's profit missed estimates as turnaround questions persist (The Business of Fashion, [Jun 25]).

EPS Upside Watch: Halfords — profit beat forecasts with margins at a decade high (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jun 25]), and it sees fiscal 2027 profit near the top end of estimates (Reuters, [Jun 25]). Callaway Golf — raised full-year guidance (TIKR.com, [Jun 24]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Meme energy has not faded: Wendy's surged over 40% after a viral Reddit post (New York Post, [Jun 24]), and GameStop is trending again. In parts of the sector, retail flows still set prices ahead of earnings.
Narrative: Mixed: grocery is in focus with Kroger and Giant Eagle trending, and staples could gain from a defensive rotation if the Q3 tech sell-off deepens; pricing power is the driver.

Reported: McCormick topped profit estimates on higher pricing (Reuters, [Jun 25]). Couche-Tard delivered its 'best performance in years' in the US, its CEO said (C-Store Dive, [Jun 24]). AB Foods led FTSE declines on a sugar warning and mixed Primark sales (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jun 30]).
EPS Upside Watch: ITC — its packaged foods business crossed $2 billion in revenue (The Economic Times, [Jun 26]), scale that can carry margins higher.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples growth is still a pricing story, not volume: Q1FY27 growth is seen steady for India's consumer staples, but driven by price (Livemint, [Jun 26]), and McCormick's beat also came on higher prices. If pricing power fades, the defensive bid has little earnings growth behind it.

Narrative: Mixed: there is no strong sector-specific signal; healthcare's defensive profile makes it a candidate for the rotation out of growth into value and quality, with the VIX at 16.35, though a 10Y at 4.47% and a hawkish Fed hold keep a lid on multiples.
Reported: No major reports this week.
EPS Upside Watch: IDEXX Laboratories — raised its 2026 EPS outlook to $15 (TIKR.com, [Jun 25]), with the diagnostics franchise compounding earnings.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Employers dropping obesity-drug coverage may help the cash-pay channel rather than shrink demand: Hims' obesity drug business may get a boost (Reuters, [Jun 25]). Coverage cuts move patients to direct-to-consumer platforms instead of removing them.

Narrative: Bearish: copper at 6.18 (↓7.1% vs 4W) trades as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, so its slide tracks the semiconductor sell-off. The cyclical drag is China's property sector, where real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May.
Reported: Evonik raised guidance on higher prices and cost reductions (WSJ, [Jun 26]). Harita Nickel posted stronger earnings on higher Q1 nickel sales volumes (Petromindo, [Jun 26]).
EPS Upside Watch: PetChem — Petronas' buyout of the PPC stake is seen lifting its earnings (NST Online, [Jun 30]), removing an earnings drag (The Star, [Jun 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Copper miners still price the AI data-centre and grid build-out rather than the 4W slide: a miner fund is up 115% in a year as copper is cast as 'the new crude' (24/7 Wall St., [Jun 28]). The equity bid is structural even while the metal falls.

Narrative: Bearish: mortgage rates near 6.5% and a rising 10Y at 4.47% are a direct headwind to REITs and affordability; the RBA's warning on the budget's influence on housing makes it a global theme.

Reported: KB Home's stock jumped after Q2 (The Motley Fool, [Jun 24]), though results point to a scale-versus-execution debate (HousingWire, [Jun 25]). UK homebuilder Berkeley called for a tax and regulatory rethink after a 15% profit fall (Reuters, [Jun 24]). Tosei REIT's distribution hit a record ¥3,926 for a fourth straight term (finance.biggo.com, [Jun 29]).

EPS Upside Watch: Industrial REITs — MBSB sees them benefiting from data-centre spin-offs and acquisitions (EdgeProp, [Jun 24]). Axis REIT — analysts call its latest purchase earnings-accretive (The Edge Malaysia, [Jun 26]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Builders are turning before rates do: home builder stocks show newfound technical strength (Barron's, [Jun 26]) and are pivoting to margin recovery as rates stay elevated (HousingWire, [Jun 30]). If margins rebuild without cheaper mortgages, a blanket Bearish call on housing is too blunt.

Narrative: Mixed: a 10Y at 4.47% (+2 bps vs 4W) pressures bond-proxy utilities, but AI data-centre power demand remains the structural tailwind, and YPF's storage and charging tie-up with Tesla points to more utility-adjacent build-out.
Reported: No major reports this week.
EPS Upside Watch: Adani Power — takes a 15,250 MW capacity milestone into its Q1 results on July 22 (Sahi, [Jun 29]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The political risk is moving from utilities to their largest customers: a bill in Congress would make tech companies pay AI data-centre energy costs (CNBC, [Jun 24]). That shields household bills, and utilities' rate cases, while the load growth stays.
Narrative: Mixed: eurozone disinflation (2.8%) helps purchasing power, but carmakers are caught between EV-transition costs and Chinese competition, and China is the driver that matters now.

Reported: BMW is preparing worker talks after a profit warning and China slowdown (The Manufacturer, [Jun 25]); its 1-3% profit margin is a 'wake-up call' for the industry (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 26]). Mercedes cut R&D jobs as German luxury car sales in China halved (finance.biggo.com, [Jun 29]).
